items.summary: Recommendation: do not authorize incremental discretionary growth or AI spend until attribution and unit economics are decision-grade. The available revenue window is only 2026-09-21: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission. Site-attributed income is $0 because the $4.92 aggregate row cannot be assigned to a site. AI usage from 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-25 cost $932.93 across 5,194 calls, including 230 errors; this supports AI spend reporting but not cost-to-learn or ROI. Contribution margin is not calculable because site-level revenue is zero/unknown and infrastructure, hosting, registrar, labor, and other direct costs are not supplied. Continue existing measurement and failure-repair work only; reject vanity metrics and unsupported forecasts.

Revenue claims must be limited to the dated provider facts: $4.92 aggregate commission for 2026-09-21, with $0 site-attributed income. Clicks, impressions, sessions, conversions, ordered items, and shipped items are operating metrics, not revenue or margin. The minimum measurement needed for site economics is a period-matched join of site/content identifier, tracking ID, affiliate clicks, orders, shipped items, commission, and reversals; plus site-level AI, infrastructure, hosting, domain, and other direct costs. Until that exists, cost-to-learn, contribution margin, CAC, ROI, and payback are not calculable.

The existing rc-9.com performance repair should remain blocked pending root-cause, validation, and rollback evidence. A performance score or TBT improvement is not a financial return and cannot justify additional spend without attributable revenue or a documented cost-saving outcome.
